title: Ext out of a constructible sheaf commutes with sums of ind-constructible sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian ([pqf-def-locnoeth]) and quasi-compact ([def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, with coefficient ring object $\Lambda_X$ as in [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring] or [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring], respectively. Write $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ for the category of module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]), and $D(\mathcal A)$ for its unbounded derived category ([def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). Let $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ denote the full subcategory of constructible module sheaves ([sk-def-sfb-constructible]), and let $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ denote the full subcategory of small filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$.

For $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, $q\in\mathbf Z$, and a family $(B_s)_{s\in S}$ in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ indexed by a set $S$, define $\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B)=\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}(C,B[q])$, with sheaves placed in degree zero. The natural map induced by the coprojections $B_s\to\bigoplus_{s\in S}B_s$,

$$
\bigoplus_{s\in S}\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_s)\longrightarrow\Ext^q_\Lambda\Bigl(C,\bigoplus_{s\in S}B_s\Bigr),
$$

is an isomorphism. The sum on the left is in abelian groups and the sum on the right is in $\mathcal A$.

proof.text: Let F be the additive functor singleFunctor 0 followed by shift q and additive Hom from C. Additivity preserves every finite coproduct, including the empty one. The module category already has the required finite coproducts and small colimits via its existing instances.

Use Mathlib CoproductsFromFiniteFiltered.liftToFinsetObj. Its standard finiteSubcoproductsCocone is colimiting. Given a cocone on F(B_s), descend on every preserved finite coproduct. Its naturality follows by checking every finite coprojection. Preservation of the filtered colimit then supplies a universal descent from F(coproduct B_s); singleton subsets give its coprojection equations, and finite coprojection extensionality proves uniqueness.

Apply constructible_sheaf_ext_continuity to the finite-subcoproduct diagram and its colimit cocone to obtain that the canonical filtered comparison is invertible. Thus F preserves that colimit, and Step 2 shows it preserves the given coproduct. Construct the additive-group coproduct on DirectSum explicitly with toAddMonoid. The unique isomorphism from this colimit to the mapped given cofan has underlying map precisely the displayed postcomposition homomorphism, hence that map is bijective.

statement_change.what: The blueprint leaves X unbound and states no global Noetherian convention. Its unrestricted reading is false in degree zero on a countable disjoint union of algebraically closed points. Add the Noetherian scope already required by the cited constructible Ext-continuity lemma, and bind the coefficient ring objects, ordinary derived category, IndCons and Ext explicitly; preserve both coefficient choices and every integer degree.

statement_change.counterexample: Take X = coproduct over n in N of Spec(k), k algebraically closed of characteristic different from ell; C = E_X and B_n its regular module on component n and zero elsewhere. All are affine-locally constructible. Their coproduct is C componentwise. Every finite sum of maps C -> B_n vanishes off finitely many components, whereas id_C is nonzero on every component. Therefore the degree-zero comparison is not surjective.

citers.note: Its separated finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian, by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian applied to Spec(k), and its Step 3 uses exactly the preserved all-integer Ext-sum comparison.

old_proof.text:
For a finite subset $T\subset S$, the map $\bigoplus_{s\in T}\Ext^q(C,B_s)\to\Ext^q(C,\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s)$
is an isomorphism because $\Ext^q(C,-)=\Hom(C,-[q])$ is additive and finite direct sums are biproducts.
The sum $\bigoplus_{s\in S}B_s$ is the filtered colimit, over the finite subsets $T$ ordered by
inclusion, of the sheaves $\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s$ in degree $0$. By part (1) of
[sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity],

$$
\Ext^q\Bigl(C,\bigoplus_SB_s\Bigr)=\varinjlim_T\Ext^q\Bigl(C,\bigoplus_TB_s\Bigr)
=\varinjlim_T\bigoplus_T\Ext^q(C,B_s)=\bigoplus_S\Ext^q(C,B_s),
$$

and the composite is the natural map.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-b7ec4f012 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the whole item and every cited node's statement, the blueprint sk-cor-ind-heart-ii-sums(.proof).md, the unit and chapter records, and the continuity blueprint. The added Noetherian hypothesis is a correctly documented E7 source error. The chapter puts no condition on X, and the counterexample checks out: on X = countable disjoint union of Spec k, E_X is the sum of its component pieces B_n, all constructible under the affine-local definition, and id_{E_X} is not a finite sum of maps C -> B_n, so the degree-0 map is not surjective. The fix takes exactly the Noetherian scope of the cited sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity and matches the sibling det-ind-heart-ii-vanishing. It keeps both coefficient choices and all q, and the item is not a target. The only citer, det-constructible-compactness-bounded (separated finite type over a field, hence Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, Step 3 with q=s-a), still holds. The coefficient rings p_X^*E and p_X^*Qlb, the Mod_{Λ_X} module objects, the ordinary unbounded D and Cons are the same as in the continuity lemma. Step 1: finite biproduct identities survive the additive localization and the shift; the empty set case is covered. Step 2: Fin(S) is small and filtered, and the colimit equals the categorical coproduct with no sectionwise claim. Step 3: all hypotheses of the continuity lemma are supplied (Noetherian X, constructible C, common lower degree 0, termwise colimit = coproduct), and the composite is the natural map. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses, and there is no cycle. No new nodes. The rg duplicate search over IndCons and sum nodes found no duplicate. Accepted tool_use: lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian, which only supplies the ambient abelian structure and colimits. No SGA source is used. No fixes.

theorem det_ind_heart_ii_sums
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X]
    (R : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) RingCat.{u + 1})
    [IsCommMonObj (coefficientHeartRingObj R)]
    (hR : R = Profinite.padicSubfieldCondensedRing ℓ E ∨
      R = Profinite.padicAlgClCondensedRing ℓ)
    (C : CategoryTheory.Mod
      (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (coefficientHeartRingObj R) X))
    (hC : IsConstantModelConstructible (coefficientHeartRingObj R) X C)
    (q : ℤ) (S : Type (u + 1))
    (B : S → CategoryTheory.Mod
      (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (coefficientHeartRingObj R) X))
    (hB : ∀ s : S, ObjectProperty.ind
      (IsConstantModelConstructible (coefficientHeartRingObj R) X) (B s))
    (c : Cofan B) (hc : IsColimit c) :
    Function.Bijective
      (@DirectSum.toAddMonoid S _ _ (Classical.decEq S) _ _ (fun s : S ↦
        Preadditive.rightComp ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj C)
          ((shiftFunctor _ q).map ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map (c.inj s)))) :
        (⨁ s : S,
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj C ⟶
            (shiftFunctor _ q).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (B s)))) →+
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj C ⟶
            (shiftFunctor _ q).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj c.pt)))
